description: Everyday conversation for golden-path steps 1 and 2 (meeting people at 18): greetings, asking after work, home, school, family and the news, the answers, raising a real subject, leaving, and the lie. Every part is a whole sentence American speakers said in federal transcripts (public domain: congressional hearings, the Congressional Record, NASA and U.S. House oral histories), counted also against the Library of Congress WPA life histories, 1936 to 1940. Record words are slots the game fills from the speaker's own records. Parts are grouped by the director's subject, role (ask, raise, reply, answer, lie) and choice; a group's parts are variants of one choice, never separate choices. A part's bearing (tender, guarded, glad, nervous, braced, curious, calm, from the director's bearings) is the manner its wording carries; a speaker's traits pull the engine toward the bearings they favor (data/english/calibration.json). A part with no bearing is neutral. A shared school or workplace is never an opener (owner, Oct 15, evening: batch 12 rejected): its ask and raise parts need the fact long-ago, which a record supplies only when something happened to the place or decades have passed.

slots.decider: The body that decides the question, by its level (Congress for a federal question), from data/english/said-as.json deciders.
slots.you: What the speaker calls the player to their face (their first name, or what a parent calls a child), from the family and name records.
slots.capital: The federal government as people in this state say it: by its capital, or plainly where the state goes by that name (data/english/said-as.json federal).
slots.name: A person's name from the records: someone both people know, or the listener's given name.
slots.employer: The speaker's employer, from their job record.
slots.claimed: The employer or town a lie claims instead, from a real record the speaker could name.
slots.my_employer: The player's own employer, from their job record.
slots.place: The town, as a resident says it, from the household record.
slots.my_place: The player's town, from their household record.
slots.school: A school, from the school record.
slots.years: A count of years, computed from two dated records.
slots.since: A month and year from a dated record, as people say it.
slots.my_since: The month and year the player started, from their job record.
slots.when: When something happened, from a dated record (a contact, a crime), as the director says it in passing.
slots.my_when: When the player last saw that person, from a contact record, said the same way.
slots.relation: How the speaker is related to someone, with the possessive, from the family record.
slots.topic: What happened, from a news record the speaker heard.
slots.first: The given name of someone both people know, from the person's record.
slots.year: A year from a dated record.
slots.headline: A printed or broadcast story's headline, as the paper screen words it.
slots.weekday: The day of the week, from the calendar.
slots.last-together: When two people last spent time together, as spoken.
slots.position: The speaker's new job, with its article ("a server"), from the job record's title.
slots.about: The policy question the reporter asks about, as a noun phrase that reads after 'on' or 'about', from the question's spoken name (data/english/question-names.json).
slots.to: The same question as a verb phrase that reads after 'to', from the question's spoken name (data/english/question-names.json).
slots.rival: A rival on the same ballot, by name, from their filing.
slots.president: The President's name, from the officials engine's record of who holds the office, as the opening story names them.
slots.state: The speaker's state as a sentence says it, from the place record, where the state's own law on the question is on record.
slots.town_figure: The town's own figure as a resident says it in passing (data/english/town-figures.json), from the economy engines' records against the country's.
slots.about-said: What the talk just had was about, from its first topic's record: an employer, a school, a town, a news story or a relative, as that topic said it.
slots.ran: The day a printed story ran, said in passing ("yesterday", "a few days ago"), from the story's own date.
slots.player-first: The player's first name, from their person record, said in a goodbye when the talk already named its topic.
slots.work_place: The town the speaker's employer is in, when it is not their own town, from the employer's record.
slots.my_position: The player's job, with its article ("a server"), from the job record's title.
slots.their_first: The given name of the person the player is talking to, from the person's record.
slots.president-object: The President where an object stands ("with {president-object}"): the role the first time the talk says them, then him or her (said-as, slot case; words composer, Nov 12).
slots.president-possessive: The President's, where a possessive stands: the role's possessive the first time, then his or her (said-as, slot case).
slots.start: When the speaker's shift starts today, as people say a time ("seven-thirty"), from the work-spans engine's shift.
slots.end: When the speaker's shift ends today, as people say a time, from the work-spans engine's shift.
slots.hours: How long the speaker's shift runs today ("eight hours"), from the work-spans engine's shift.
slots.wage: What the speaker's job pays an hour, as people round it ("about $18"), from the job record.
slots.against: What an opponent of the question says they want ("say no to higher tariffs"), from data/english/question-names.json against.
slots.rent: The household's rent, as people round it ("about $1,200"), from the lease record.
slots.due: When the rent is due, from today ("tomorrow", "in three days"), from the lease record.
slots.usual: How long the speaker's shift usually runs ("eight hours"), from the job record's daily hours.
slots.age: The age a person turned, from the paper's milestone birthday story.
slots.office: The office a race is for, as its contest record names it.
slots.who: An office as its holder is said again ("the governor"), from data/english/said-as.json offices.
slots.body: The local body that decided a measure, said as people say it ("the county board"), from data/english/said-as.json deciders.
slots.purpose: What a budget line is for, from the bill catalog's budget row (data/english/bill-names.json).
slots.amount: A sum of money from a record, as people round it.
slots.sponsor: The person who brought the bill a story covers, by name, from the bill's sponsor record (legislature bills).
slots.their_home: Where the person speaking lives, as a resident says it, from their household record.
slots.their_employer: The speaker's own employer, from their job record.
slots.their_years: How long the speaker has held their job, in whole years with the word ("seven years"), from the job's start record.
slots.kin_employer: Where the speaker's relative works, from the relative's job record.
slots.kin_home: Where the speaker's relative lives, from the relative's household record.

lineWords.about: A line the engine composes from parts (opener, core, reason, closer) is longer than one part: each part keeps maxWords, and the whole line keeps this many words besides its slots. Set for the address point (owner, Nov 11: the relative raises a real thing the President said and where they stand on it from their own life), which says the point, the stand and the reason in one turn.

mining.rule: A shape is kept when at least 2 documents say it as a whole sentence and one of them is a public-domain record from 2015 or later, which is its source.

secondRun.note: Parts the rebuilt corpus attests that the first run's corpus did not, merged into the first run's parts.
